name: AI Query Optimisation
title: AI Query Optimisation
answer: AI query optimisation covers the parts of a database that decide how a query is executed, including join order, access paths, cardinality estimates and configuration knobs. Classical optimisers rely on cost models and heuristics, while learned systems use statistics and past executions to predict costs, recommend indexes and tune settings automatically. The field spans research prototypes and features shipped in commercial engines, and it sits inside the broader area of AI and SQL. The central tension is that a learned choice can be accurate on average yet hard to explain when it goes wrong, which matters when a plan change causes a regression.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems run inside or alongside the database engine, so the substrate is the DBMS itself, commonly PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and cloud warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery and Redshift. Learned components may be embedded in the optimiser, exposed as extensions, or served as separate advisory services that read query logs and telemetry. The Model Context Protocol has become a common way to connect AI assistants to these systems: this site tracks 2511 active MCP servers, 263 of them for SQL databases and warehouses. The site's own pages are built from a PostgreSQL database, which is a reminder that the same engine being optimised is often the one holding the metadata.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work usually starts with query logs, execution plans and runtime counters, which are cleaned and featurised before any model is trained. Common approaches include regression for cardinality estimation, reinforcement learning or learned cost models for join ordering, and bandit methods for configuration tuning, with evaluation on standard benchmarks such as TPC-H, TPC-DS and the Join Order Benchmark. Models are typically trained offline and then deployed either as advisors that rank plans or as components that sit inside the optimiser loop. The site's library holds 288 research papers, a portion of which cover learned query optimisation, and the field is small enough that a single paper can shift practice.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance matters because query logs and plan caches often contain literal values, table names and user identifiers that may be sensitive or regulated. A learned optimiser that changes plans silently can be difficult to audit, so teams need versioned models, recorded inputs and a way to fall back to a classical plan. Rights and licensing also apply to the training data and to any third party model or service used in the loop. The risk is not only a slow query, it is an unexplained regression that is hard to reproduce, which is why explainability and rollback are treated as first class concerns.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Learned components are moving from research prototypes into mainstream engines, often as optional features that advise the classical optimiser rather than replace it. Expect more work on explainability, on benchmarks that test robustness to distribution shift, and on standard ways to package a learned optimiser for reuse. The MCP ecosystem for SQL is likely to keep growing, which will make it easier for AI assistants to inspect plans and suggest changes. The open question is whether learned optimisation becomes a default part of the database or remains a specialist add on for workloads where the gains justify the opacity.
